PerEpochTokens, when set, also bounds the spend since the graph's
current epoch started (a reset starts a new epoch). 1..1e12.

epoch.description: Epoch is the graph's current epoch, which per_epoch_tokens counts.

per_epoch_tokens.description:
PerEpochTokens and the two fields after it are present only when the
budget has a per-epoch limit: the graph's tokens since its current
epoch started, and what is left of that limit (never below 0).

remaining.description: Remaining is monthly_tokens - used, never below 0.

resets_at.description: ResetsAt is the next 1st of the month, 00:00 UTC.

used.description: Used is the graph's tokens (input + output) this UTC month.

archived_at.description:
Review resolution (migration 020, contract §10). ArchivedAt is set by
merge/discard (or the losing side of a contradiction pair): the row is
out of every read but never deleted. Resolution records how a curator
closed this row's review item; ResolvedContradictions lists the older
observations whose contradiction with this row has been resolved.

contradicts.description:
Contradicts lists existing observations on the same node this one
contradicts (P >= judgment.AlignContradictionMin at judgment time). Not a
foreign key: the record that a contradiction was found outlives the row.

kind.description: Kind is finding | decision | summary | brief (migration 101).

node_id.description: NodeID is empty for a graph-scoped observation (migration 101).

review.description:
Review marks a judged POSSIBLE duplicate of MergedInto: stored, flagged
for a human. A row the judgment called the same fact is never stored, so
MergedInto is only ever set together with Review (migration 014 CHECK).

support.description:
Support is grounded | asserted | decision | unjudged (migration 023):
whether this fact is a measurement, a hunch, a recorded choice, or
unjudged. A LABEL, never a gate — an asserted row is stored exactly as
before. It travels on every read so a later agent can tell a hunch from a
measurement instead of treating both as established, which is the whole
point: observations are re-served as context on every claim.

candidates.description:
Candidates is how many existing observations were compared: the most
recent, at most judgment.MaxCandidates.

contradicts_weaker.description:
ContradictsWeaker is the subset of Contradicts that this observation
OUTWEIGHS: rows it disagrees with that are merely asserted, while this
one is grounded. Without it a contradiction says only "these disagree"
and a reader cannot tell which to believe — which is the whole reason
the support pair exists.

decision.description:
Decision is the alignment level, which IS the action: stored (distinct,
201), review (possible duplicate, 201 with review=true and merged_into
set), merged (the same fact, 200 with the EXISTING row and nothing
stored).

meaning.description:
Meaning spells out the contradiction in a sentence, because the ids alone
do not tell an agent what to do about them.

support.description:
Support is what this fact was judged to be: grounded (checkable and the
attached record shows it), asserted (checkable, nothing shows it),
decision (a choice or intention, with no external fact to check), or
unjudged.

account_id.description:
AccountID finished it (its last succeeded run's created_by); absent
when no run recorded who.

at.description: At is when it was finished (the prerequisite's ended_at).

node_id.description: NodeID and Title are the prerequisite finished last.

email.description: Email is present only when v3 sent it — for a caller holding AdminRead.

cooldown_seconds.description:
CooldownSeconds is the wait after completion before the reset
(completion only; 0..315360000; absent means 0).

every_seconds.description:
EverySeconds is the schedule interval, counted from the epoch's start
(schedule only; 60..315360000).

force.description:
Force: whether a loop reset cancels running runs. False skips a busy
graph and retries next tick.

max_epochs.description: MaxEpochs stops the loop once epoch >= max_epochs; null is unbounded.

on.description: On is what triggers a reset: the graph completing, or a fixed interval.

cooldown_seconds.description:
CooldownSeconds is the wait after completion before the reset
(completion only; 0..315360000; absent means 0).

every_seconds.description:
EverySeconds is the schedule interval, counted from the epoch's start
(schedule only; 60..315360000).

force.description:
Force: whether a loop reset cancels running runs. False skips a busy
graph and retries next tick.

max_epochs.description: MaxEpochs stops the loop once epoch >= max_epochs; null is unbounded.

on.description: On is what triggers a reset: the graph completing, or a fixed interval.

frontier.description:
Frontier is what became runnable once this run closed, computed in the
SAME transaction — so it reflects this outcome rather than a state that
existed before it. Under a gate policy the node is held in `verifying`
(its dependents are not in this list) and the frontier is recomputed
after the verdict moves it: to done, releasing them, or to failed.

NOT CLAIMED. Reading is deliberate: a harness that crashes between this
response and starting work would otherwise hold claims on nodes it never
began, and there is no reaper. Call /frontier/claim when actually ready.

warnings.description:
Warnings are advisories about the caller's client (migration 089);
see ClaimResponse.Warnings.

actor_client_id.description:
Attribution (migration 076, AGENTS_CONTRACT §9), stamped from the
credential that claimed the run and again from the one that completed
it when that one carried attribution. All three absent for an ordinary
credential and on runs before 076. Attribution only: nothing grants on
them; self-judgment refuses on OnBehalfOf.

ActorClientID is Tier 1: the OAuth client that acted AS created_by.

agent_id.description:
AgentID is Tier 2: the v3 agent whose credential was presented;
created_by is then that agent's service account.

client.description:
Client is the X-Graph-Client the harness sent (migration 089), e.g.
`enforcer-graph-plugin/0.14.0; hooks=on`. Null when no request of this
run carried the header - never a fabricated value.

epoch.description: the graph's epoch when the run opened (043); attempt counts across epochs

epoch_attempt.description:
EpochAttempt and FailedAttempts are the claim card's per-epoch numbers
(contract §5), present ONLY on the run POST .../runs just opened, so
StartRun answers what the two claim endpoints answer. Never on a list.

evidence.description:
Evidence is what the harness attached to SHOW the work happened
(§2a, migration 022). Raw so the scan list stays one line per column;
EvidenceOf decodes it. Absent on runs that attached nothing and on
every run that ended before 022.

judgment_pending_since.description:
JudgmentPendingSince is set while the run waits for the worker's Jev
call (docs/JUDGMENT_CONTRACT.md §12, migration 067): its verdict (the
plain path, where verification.state is `pending`), Jev's vote (a
validated run) or its typed outputs (validation with no Jev seat).
Absent once the worker wrote it, and on every run that owed no call.

on_behalf_of.description:
OnBehalfOf is the human answerable for the run: the agent's steward, or
created_by itself under an act claim.

outcome.description:
Outcome is a server-known outcome beyond status (migration 093): only
`landing_blocked` today (the work is done, its PR could not land), with
PRURL and LandingReason. Absent on every ordinary run.

outputs.description:
Outputs are the node's declared outputs as the judge decided them in
the verification call (docs/OUTPUTS_AND_LINKS_CONTRACT.md §2), keyed by
output name. Absent when nothing was declared or no call was made.

usage.description:
Usage is what the run spent (migration 088): null for a worker that
reported none - never coerced to zero. While the run is running it is
the harness's last heartbeat total; completion supersedes it.

validation.description:
Validation is the run's validation-v1 state (docs/VALIDATION_CONTRACT.md
§8) when its graph had a validation config at completion: the judges
drawn, the quorum, the tally and the outcome. Absent otherwise.

verdict_resolution.description:
Verdict resolution by a curator (migration 020, contract §10): accept
keeps the verdict and stops the worker re-judging; rejudge asked for a
fresh one. Cleared whenever a new verdict is written.

verification.description:
Verification is the judgment verdict once the run ended and judgment
ran (docs/JUDGMENT_CONTRACT.md §2). Absent while running and on runs
that ended before judgment existed.

source.description:
Source: reported (the provider's own counters) or estimated (the
harness's guess). Defaults to reported when omitted.

turns.description:
Turns is the run's model turns so far (a running total, like the rest).
Optional; the graph's node_caps.max_turns is checked against it.

message.example: no X-Graph-Client header: heartbeats, evidence and usage are not being captured

reason.description: Reason is the text after `hooks=off:` when the client gave one.

pinned_version.description:
PinnedVersion nil means "follow the latest published version". A value
pins, which is what makes a graph an agent walks reproducible instead of
drifting when someone publishes a new version underneath it.

position.description:
Position is the load order and is therefore part of the contract, not
decoration.

source.description:
Source says where the attachment came from on a node's resolved list:
"graph" (a graph-level skill matching the node's type, migration 092)
or "node" (attached to this node). Graph-level skills load first.

description.description:
Description is how an agent decides whether to load the body at all, so it
is required rather than optional.
description.example: Run build, vet and tests before calling anything done.

previous_judges.description:
PreviousJudges are the first vote's judges (and "jev" when Jev sat):
none of them holds a seat in the re-opened vote.

previous_tally.description: PreviousTally is the first vote's tally.

rejected_at.description: RejectedAt is when the appealed rejection was decided.

arbitrators.description:
Arbitrators are explicit grants IN ADDITION to the graph owner and
tenant admins, who always arbitrate.

deadline_seconds.description:
DeadlineSeconds: a run still undecided this long after it entered
validation escalates (reason `deadline`). 60..2592000; absent means
86400.

jev.description:
Jev: Jev is one of the n judges, its vote the graph's approval
policy's aggregate (accept, reject, or undecided inside the band).

reason.description:
Reason is why the last attempt cast nothing: unavailable, key_unusable,
token_cap, check_error.

verdict_id.description:
VerdictID is the run_verdicts row (applied = false) holding Jev's
aggregate — the approval policy's verdict this vote was read from.

vote.description: Vote is accept, reject or undecided; absent while uncast.

groups.description:
Groups are v3 group SLUGS naming live groups in the caller's tenant.
Each is BOUND to its v3 group id when the config is written (063), and
is one seat in the draw, filled by whichever member of THAT group (by
id) votes first — never by a later group that took the slug.

scope.description:
Scope: private (owner + accounts/groups), workspace (owner + graph
members + accounts/groups; the graph must be tenant-visible),
allowlist (only accounts/groups; at least one), none (no people;
Jev alone: requires jev and n = 1).

from.description: From is the quorum's decision the arbitrator overturned.

m.description: M: how many must agree. ceil(n/2) <= m <= n, so a minority never decides.

n.description: N: judges assigned to each run. 1..15.

appeal.description:
Appeal is set once the run's producer appealed a rejection (§6a): the
vote was re-opened with fresh seats, excluding PreviousJudges.

assigned.description:
Assigned are the judges drawn at random for this run: account ids and
"group:<slug>" seats (any member of that group may fill one).

config.description:
Config is the graph's config AS IT WAS when this run entered
validation: editing the graph's config never changes a vote in flight.

deadline_at.description:
DeadlineAt is when a still-pending run escalates for `deadline`:
opened_at + config.deadline_seconds. Computed, never stored (045's
validation_deadline_at is the stored rule).

decided_by.description:
DecidedBy is quorum on a vote's decision, arbitrator once an escalated
run was approved or rejected; null while pending or escalated.

escalated_at.description: EscalatedAt is when the run escalated; absent otherwise.

filled.description:
Filled maps each seat that has voted to the account that filled it,
so one group seat is filled once.

jev.description:
Jev is Jev's seat, present once Jev was asked: the vote it cast (or
the attempts that could not cast one). Absent when jev is false.

jev_reason.description:
JevReason and WeakestCriterion are present only on a completion
response whose run Jev voted to reject (§5): the reason on Jev's
verdict (no_evidence, unsupported_by_evidence, check_failed …) and the
text of its lowest-P(met) criterion, so a worker learns why while it
still holds the context. Read from Jev's own verdict, never stored here.

override.description:
Override is set once an arbitrator overturned the quorum's decision
(§6a): who, when, the note and the decision overturned. DecidedBy is
then arbitrator.

reason.description:
Reason is set when escalated: pool_too_small (fewer eligible judges
than n when validation opened), deadline, or jev_undecided (Jev's vote
is undecided and the uncast seats can reach neither m accepts nor
n − m + 1 rejects).

superseded_by_decision.description:
SupersededByDecision is set once an arbitrator decided the run's gate
node through POST /nodes/{id}/decide (§6b): the deciding run and when.
An open block is closed then as state `superseded`.

evidence.description: Evidence is the evidence so far. Absent: the run's captured evidence.

report.description: Report is the progress claim. Absent: the run's data.report.

confidence.description: Confidence is the judge's confidence in Score, 0..1.

criteria.description:
Criteria carries one P(met) per judged criterion, same order as the
run's frozen acceptance (check rows are not evaluated here).

state.description:
State is judged (the judge answered), unsupported (no evidence: no call
was made), or skipped (see Reason).

would_verify.description: WouldVerify says whether this evidence would pass the verdict rule now.

signatures.description:
Signatures is the A2A v1.0 §8.4 AgentCardSignature list (contract
§1a): one detached ES256 JWS over the JCS-canonical card without this
member, kid in the protected header. Absent when no signing keyring is
configured (GRAPH_A2A_SIGNING_KEYS).

accounts.description:
Accounts is the union of creator, members and every resolved group's
members: one row per account, at its highest role, saying how it is
held. Group members appear only for groups whose members.status is ok.

creator.description: Creator is null when graphs.created_by is unknown.

groups_unresolved.description:
GroupsUnresolved is true when accounts may be incomplete: a BOUND
group grant's members could not be listed for this request (members
status unavailable, forbidden, unconfigured or skipped), or v3 listed
fewer members than its total. The response is still 200; nothing is
granted or refused by it. An unbound grant, or a group v3 no longer has
(unknown_group), grants nobody and does not set it.

guests.description:
Guests are the people the plan sent work to by email (GVNR guest
links), each by the name the sender gave on the newest link, revoked
links included: their steps and tasks keep that name after the link
goes, and a reused address shows the new name, not its account's old
one. Display text the sender typed. Omitted when none.

mix.description:
Mix counts the plan's people and the companies they come from (by
work email domain); counts only, never a domain. Absent when the
directory could not be read.

names_unavailable.description:
NamesUnavailable is true when enforcer-v3's directory could not be read
for this request, so the creator and legacy members it should name are
unnamed for now (not nameless): ask again rather than show them as
"someone". Still 200; omitted when false.

meta.description:
Meta describes accounts[] after q, limit and offset. total ignores
offset. On a plain GET (no q, no limit) total is every account, client
seats included. limit is the cap, or total when limit was omitted.

group_id.description:
GroupID and GroupSlug name the granted group; present for share and
group only.

kind.description:
Kind: creator (the graph's creator) | member (a legacy per-account
share) | share (a member of one of the graph's per-DAG sharing groups)
| group (a member of an ordinary granted v3 group).

Kind is accounts.kind: human, or service (an agent's identity). Absent
when v3's directory could not say (unreadable, or not in the caller's
tenant).

steward.description:
Steward is the human answerable for an agent; present only for a
service account whose agent the caller may view in v3 (AgentService).

username.description:
Username, FirstName, LastName and Email are what v3 returned for this
account in the first group's members that listed it, after v3's own
redaction, never enriched. An account no group listed (creator or legacy
member only) is filled from v3's directory under the caller's scope, by
the same rules: only for a credential that could read a v3 group member
list (unscoped or a coarse enforcer scope, never a portal link), in the
caller's tenant only, email only for a caller with tenant read. Absent
when v3 has none or the lookup failed.

via.description:
Via lists how the role is held: creator first, then a legacy member
row, then groups in groups[] order.

group_id.description:
GroupID is the stored grant's group_id, else the id resolved from v3 for
this request (never stored). Absent when neither is known.

kind.description:
Kind is "share" for one of the graph's own per-DAG sharing groups
(graph-<graph-id>-viewers|editors|admins, managed through
/graphs/{id}/members — the people the graph is shared with) and "group"
for an ordinary v3 group granted through /graphs/{id}/groups.

items.description: Items are at most 1,000 members, after v3's redaction; empty unless ok.

status.description:
Status: ok | unavailable (timeout or 5xx) | forbidden (v3 401/403) |
unknown_group (404, or the grant is bound to no group id) | unconfigured
(GRAPH_V3_BASE_URL empty) | skipped (past the 20-group cap).

total.description: Total is v3's member count; null unless status is ok.

companies.description:
Companies counts distinct work email domains among the people. A
personal mailbox (gmail.com, outlook.com, ...) or an unknown email adds
no company; at least 1 whenever there is a person.

tenant_wide_readers.description:
TenantWideReaders: accounts whose platform role reads every graph in the
tenant (TenantRead), and so see this one without any row below.

tenant_wide_writers.description:
TenantWideWriters: accounts whose platform role writes every graph in the
tenant (TenantWrite), and so are ADMIN on this one without any row below.

inherited.description:
Inherited and Shadowed appear on graph lists only: a tenant-wide row is
inherited; one a live graph-scoped profile of the same name overrides is
also shadowed.

kind.description:
Kind is agent_key (secret = an ag_ credential) or client_credentials
(client_id and client_secret of an agent-bound OAuth client).

scheme.description:
Scheme "client_credentials" makes the bridge mint a token at token_url
(client_id, client_secret, optional scope) instead of sending credentials.

eligible.description: Eligible: enough decided runs (3) for the routing fallback to use it.

rate.description: Rate is verified / (verified + rejected); null with no decided run.

file_id.description:
FileID is the enforcer-files export copy; empty when the upload did not
succeed. The pack itself is served by GET /graphs/{id}/context/pack.

file_exported.description:
FileExported is true when the enforcer-files export copy exists
(pack.file_id is set). A failed upload does not fail the rebuild.

truncated.description: Truncated lists the sections (2..5) the cap cut.

unchanged.description:
Unchanged is true when the content hash matched the stored pack, so
nothing was uploaded and file_id is the existing one.

type.description:
Type is the predicate. Defaults to "relates_to"; use the graph's
dependency_edge_type ("requires" by default) for scheduling edges.

Type retypes the edge (e.g. requires -> relates_to retires a stale
dependency without a delete). Omitted or equal to the current type: no
change. A real change records retyped_from / retyped_at / retyped_by in
the edge's data.

asked_by.description: AskedBy and SentTo are first names ("" when GVNR cannot name them).

kind.description:
Kind is money (a money ask), sign_off, or invite (an invite to a
plan, sent by GVNR to an email address).

open.description:
Open is false once it was decided (or the task moved on, or the invite
was revoked or ran out): nothing to do.

what.description:
What is the ask's line ("£40 more to finish Chase invoices") or the
task that needs the sign-off.

decision.description:
Decision is what was decided, 1..200 characters. When the gate declares
data.options it must equal one of them.

follow_ups.description:
FollowUps are node keys the decider wants worked next; recorded on the
evidence item, nothing is created or claimed.

note.description: Note is optional context for the decision, at most 4000 characters.

protocol.description: Protocol is the worker protocol version (docs/PROTOCOL.md §8).

file_name.description: FileName is the SAME value given to upload-url.

role.description:
Role is the caller's own role on the folder: read | write | manage |
service, exactly as enforcer-files' folderaccess resolves it for THIS
request — never cached, never derived from the graph role alone.

complete_url.description:
CompleteURL is THIS service's public path for the second step
(POST /graphs/{id}/files/complete), never enforcer-files' in-cluster
address: PUT the bytes to upload_url, then POST {"file_name": "..."}
here under the SAME credential to record the upload.

expiry_seconds.description:
ExpirySeconds bounds the presigned URL's lifetime (enforcer-files'
default 900, max 604800). 0 uses that default.

file_name.description: FileName is the target path within the folder, e.g. "evidence/a.pdf".

overwrite.description: Overwrite allows replacing the CALLER's own existing file at that path.

assignee_group_slug.description:
AssigneeGroupSlug assigns the node to a group (contract §10); a slug,
never an account id.

links.description:
Links carries every OTHER outgoing relation, keyed by edge type — a
knowledge graph's 'cites' or 'relates_to'. Also from this node outwards,
so it cannot be inverted either.

requires.description:
Requires lists the node keys this node depends on. Reads as
"pass-1-read requires pass-0-schema".

dependency_edge_type.description:
DependencyEdgeType names the scheduling relation and defaults to
'requires'. It is what `requires:` on a node becomes.

lifecycle.description:
Lifecycle is "terminal" (the default: the graph completes once per
epoch) or "open" (it never completes). Anything else is 400
invalid_lifecycle.

loop.description:
Loop, when present, is set on the built graph exactly as PUT
/graphs/{graphId}/loop would set it, with the importer as set_by. A
set_by in the document is refused. on=completion with lifecycle open is
400 loop_requires_terminal.

mode.description:
Mode defaults to dag. 'graph' permits cycles, for a knowledge graph where
they are natural.

node_defaults.description:
NodeDefaults is the built graph's per-node-type defaults (migration
092; the shape PATCH /graphs/{graphId} takes). The document's nodes get
their type's defaults for every field they omit.

slug.description:
Slug and Name override the document's own when set, so one document can
seed a dev, a staging and a prod graph without being edited three times.

joined_workspace.description:
JoinedWorkspace: the caller was signed in to another workspace, and
enforcer-v3 admitted them to this one (tenant_id) to accept it. The plan
is shared with their account there; they switch to it to see the plan.

node_id.description: NodeID: a one-step invite's task, for the client to open the plan on.

role.description:
Role is the invite's role when shared is true, else the role the caller
already held, which was at least the invite's.

shared.description:
Shared is false when the caller already held the invite's role or
higher: nothing changed, and an invite never lowers a role.

group_id.description:
GroupID is an optional ASSERTION: the v3 group the caller means. The
service resolves the slug itself and never trusts this; when both are
given and the slug now names a different group, the request is refused
with 409 group_id_mismatch instead of binding to the newcomer.

group_slug.description:
GroupSlug must name a live enforcer-v3 group in the caller's tenant, as
the caller's own credential sees it; the grant binds to that group's id.

client_policy.description:
ClientPolicy: off | warn (default) | require (migration 089). Anything
else is 400 invalid_body.

default_lease_seconds.description:
DefaultLeaseSeconds defaults to 300. 30..86400. Raise it for a graph whose
nodes are long agent runs; a node can still override it individually.

dependency_edge_type.description:
DependencyEdgeType names the edge type that expresses scheduling. The
direction is fixed: an edge reads dependent --<type>--> prerequisite.
Defaults to "requires".

description.description: Description is free prose shown in listings.

lifecycle.description:
Lifecycle is "terminal" (the default: the graph completes once per
epoch) or "open" (it never completes and is appended to forever).
Anything else is 400 invalid_lifecycle.

min_client_version.description:
MinClientVersion is X.Y.Z; a client below it gets client_outdated, and
under require its claim is refused.

mode.description:
Mode is "dag" (acyclicity enforced on every edge write, and topology and
frontier are available) or "graph" (cycles permitted, ordering endpoints
refuse). Defaults to "dag".

node_defaults.description:
NodeDefaults: per-node-type defaults (see Graph.NodeDefaults). Keys of
each entry: outputs (array), checks (array of {"check": ...} rows),
tier (mechanical|standard|deep), profile (string). Anything else is
400 invalid_body naming it.

verification_policy.description:
VerificationPolicy overrides the tenant's judgment policy for this graph:
"advisory" stores a verdict and leaves the node done; "gate" moves a
rejected node back to failed. Omitted inherits the tenant setting.

visibility.description:
Visibility "tenant" makes the graph readable by anyone in the tenant with
tenant-wide read; "private" (the default) restricts it to its creator and
explicit members.

account_id.description: AccountID: an account already in this workspace, instead of an email.

days.description: Days until the link stops working: 1..30, default 14.

email.description:
Email is the guest's address. Required unless account_id names someone
already in this workspace.

name.description:
Name is who the link is for, 1..60 characters: their seat and receipts
show it ("Olivia (guest link)").

node_ids.description:
NodeIDs are the tasks of this plan the guest may take, finish and add a
note to (at most 20). Requests put to the guest on this plan are always
in scope, so a link for requests alone may list none.

note.description:
Note is what the sender wants the person to know (at most 1000
characters): a task passed by email shows it in the email, quoted.
note.example: The March ones look off to me

email.description:
Email: GVNR emails the invite to this address itself (133), in GVNR's
own look, with a verify code. Optional; without it nothing is sent and
the caller shares the link. 20 emails an hour per sender (429
invite_email_limit); the same address on the same plan (and step)
within a day is not emailed twice (email.status already_sent). 503
invite_email_unavailable when GVNR cannot send (no seal key).

expires_in_hours.description:
ExpiresInHours is how long the link works. Default 168 (7 days), at
most 720 (30 days).

for_name.description:
ForName is who the invite is for, as the inviter typed it (1..60
characters after trimming): display text only, never checked against
who opens it.

node_id.description:
NodeID makes a one-step invite: a task of this graph the person is
asked to do. Joining is the same; the plan then opens on that task.

note.description: Note is the inviter's own words in the email (1..500 characters).
note.example: Could you check the supplier invoices by Friday?

role.description:
Role the invite shares the plan at. Default viewer, as the link works
for anyone who has it; ask for editor, which taking, finishing and
assigning work need.

seat.description:
Seat "auditor" makes an auditor invite: always viewer (role must be
empty or viewer), and whoever uses it is seated as the plan's auditor,
read-only (receipts, decisions, the evidence pack, Verify links).

expires_in_hours.description:
ExpiresInHours is how long the link works. Default 720 (30 days), at
most 8760 (a year). 0 is refused rather than read as the default.

email.description: Email is present when the request asked GVNR to email the invite.

for_name.description: ForName: who it is for, as the inviter typed it. Display text.

node_id.description:
NodeID: a one-step invite's task (absent for a plain invite, or when
the task was deleted since).

status.description:
Status is active until expires_at passes (expired) or an editor
revokes it (revoked, which wins).

token.description:
Token is the secret the link carries. Shown once; send it to people,
never log it.

url.description:
URL is the portal link: GRAPH_INVITE_URL_BASE + /login#invite=<token>.
The token is in the fragment, which a browser never sends to a server.
With no base configured it is that path alone, relative to the portal.

status.description:
Status is active until expires_at passes (expired) or an editor
revokes it (revoked, which wins).

token.description: Token is the secret the link carries. Shown once; never log it.

url.description:
URL is GRAPH_PLAN_LINK_URL_BASE + /p/<token> (default base
https://mcp.gvnr.io): the page to paste into an AI or send to someone.

kind.description:
Kind: guest (an editor made it) or email (a one-tap button in a GVNR
email to a plan member, made by the notifier for that one task).

token.description: Token is the guest's credential (a v3 portal link). Shown once; never log it.

url.description:
URL is GRAPH_INVITE_URL_BASE + /gvnr/g#<token>: the token rides in the
fragment, which no browser sends to a server.

buttons.description:
Buttons is the caller's choice for one-tap buttons in their emails
("Start it", "Done", "I'm stuck", "Looks good", "Send it back"):
on ("I don't use AI, just email me"), off ("I use AI now"), or auto
(on until GVNR sees them act through an AI app).

buttons_on.description: ButtonsOn is what that means today for their emails.

off.description:
Off are the kinds of email the caller turned off, for every plan:
assigned (a task was given to you), vote (your approval is needed),
ready (your task can start), sent_back (your task was sent back),
still_waiting (a task is waiting for a decision), question (someone
asked you a question), answered (your question was answered), overdue
(your task is past its due date), or all. Sorted. Summary emails are
set per plan, on PUT /graphs/{graphId}/digest.

approval.description:
Approval overrides the tenant's approval policy for this graph, key by
key (docs/OUTPUTS_AND_LINKS_CONTRACT.md §10). Absent means inherit.

can.description:
Can is what Role lets the caller do, from graphauth.Capabilities — the
one table GET /graphs/{id}/access also reads. Set wherever Role is.

client_policy.description:
ClientPolicy is what the graph does about a worker whose X-Graph-Client
is missing or below MinClientVersion (migration 089): off emits nothing,
warn (default) adds `warnings` to claim/heartbeat/complete responses,
require refuses the claim with 409 client_attestation_required.

code.description:
Code is the plan's short code (migration 142): three characters from
23456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ (four once the workspace has used every
three-character one), never GV first, unique within the workspace,
fixed for the plan's life and never given to another plan there. It
only points: GET /plan-codes/{code} opens the plan for a person on it.

confidential.description:
Confidential is true on a plan whose people are added by name only
(migration 115): no invite link or plan link can be made or used, no
AI judge (jev) sits on its approvals, and no team notices webhook
posts its titles. Set through PATCH /graphs/{graphId} (admin).

context.description:
Context is the graph's shared-context settings (migration 101,
docs/GRAPH_MEMORY_CONTRACT.md): {"recall": {"enabled": false, "limit": 8}}.
`{}` means every default: include=recall on a claim is empty.

default_lease_seconds.description:
DefaultLeaseSeconds is how long a claim holds a node in this graph before
another harness may take it, unless the node overrides it. A harness that
stops heartbeating within this window has its node returned to the
frontier instead of stalling the plan forever (migration 010).

effective_client_policy.description:
EffectiveClientPolicy is the policy that applies: the graph's own.
The platform never raises a graph to require; set it per graph once the
plugin ships attestation everywhere.

effective_min_client_version.description:
EffectiveMinClientVersion is the graph's own min_client_version, else the
platform default (env GRAPH_DEFAULT_MIN_CLIENT_VERSION). Set on GET only.

epoch.description: Epoch is the current epoch, 1 until the first reset (contract §2).

idle.description:
Idle is true when the graph has at least one live node and its work
roll-up (GET /graphs/{id}/summary's `state`) is complete, waiting or
stalled: nothing claimable, nothing claimed, nothing validating. A
complete terminal graph is idle; a graph-mode graph never is. Computed
on getGraph only; omitted from listGraphs.

judgment_budget.description:
JudgmentBudget bounds the judgment tokens this graph may spend
(migration 072), under the tenant's monthly cap, which still applies.
Absent means none: the graph spends the tenant's cap. Set through
PATCH /graphs/{graphId} (admin); what is left is on
GET /graphs/{graphId}/judgment/usage's budget block.

lifecycle.description:
Lifecycle: a terminal graph completes once per epoch; an open one never
completes (docs/REPLAY_AND_QUERY_CONTRACT.md §1). Graphs that predate
migration 043 are terminal.

loop.description:
Loop is the graph's reset loop; null means manual resets only
(contract §4). Read-only here: it is set through the loop endpoints.
Reads carry set_by (the account that wrote it); writes refuse it.

mandates.description:
Mandates are criteria appended to every run's frozen acceptance list in
this graph, after the node's own and before the tenant's (migration
040), and judged like any criterion. Absent means none.

min_client_version.description:
MinClientVersion is the oldest client version (X.Y.Z) the graph accepts
without a client_outdated warning; absent means any.

needs_me.description:
NeedsMe rides on a row only with work=needs_me: what waits on the
caller on this plan (graph_needs_me_for, 139; the overview's
me.needs_me adds these up over the same plans).

node_caps.description:
NodeCaps is the most one node's run may spend (migration 156): a run
that reports usage over it is marked over_cap and a node_over_cap review
item opens. Null = no cap. Set through PATCH /graphs/{graphId}.

node_defaults.description:
NodeDefaults is how this graph's nodes are delivered, keyed by node
type (migration 092): {"task": {"outputs": [...], "checks":
[{"check": ...}], "tier": "standard", "profile": "<routing profile>"}}.
A node created without one of those fields gets its type's default
(recorded as data.node_defaults_applied); the claim card merges them at
read time for nodes that predate the default. `{}` means none.

notify_holds.description:
NotifyHolds is true on a plan whose judge holds (a verdict pending, a
low-confidence or plain rejection, an unverified verdict, an uncertain
output) are emailed to the owner, the task's assignee and the
arbitrators (migration 150). Off by default. Set through PATCH
/graphs/{graphId}.

progress.description:
Progress and Complete ride on a row only when asked for: include=progress,
hide_complete or sort=progress on listGraphs. Status counts only.

verification_policy.description:
VerificationPolicy overrides the tenant's judgment policy for this graph
(docs/JUDGMENT_CONTRACT.md §4). Absent means inherit the tenant setting.

work_counts.description:
WorkCounts rides on a row only with include=work_counts: ready,
running, gates and needs_me on this plan, read for the page only.

every.description:
Every is how often the caller gets a summary email of this plan:
daily or weekly, at 07:00 in Tz, or off.

tz.description:
Tz is the caller's zone (an IANA name, default UTC): summaries go at
07:00 there, and overdue emails count days there. One zone per
person, across every plan.

for_name.description: ForName: who it is for, as the inviter typed it. Display text.

node_id.description:
NodeID: a one-step invite's task (absent for a plain invite, or when
the task was deleted since).

status.description:
Status is active until expires_at passes (expired) or an editor
revokes it (revoked, which wins).

meta.description:
Meta repeats limit, offset and total. Data.Total stays for older
clients; both count the rows under q and status, whatever the offset.

for_name.description: ForName: who the inviter wrote it for. Display text, never identity.

graph_name.description:
GraphName is set by the plan's editors: display text, not proof of
which plan it is.

invited_by_first_name.description:
InvitedByFirstName is the inviter's own enforcer-v3 first name. They
set it themselves, so show it quoted, as display text, never as who
they are. Absent when they have none, the directory could not be read,
or the credential could not read a v3 group member list itself (a fine
scope).

invited_by_username.description:
InvitedByUsername is the inviter's enforcer-v3 username, under the same
rules. They chose it too, but it is unique in the workspace, so no one
else can show it: it tells two people with one first name apart.

other_workspace.description:
OtherWorkspace: the invite is for another workspace than the caller's
(tenant_id). Accepting asks enforcer-v3 to admit them there, under its
rules, and they join it as well as the plan.

role.description: Role is the role accepting shares the plan at.

seat.description: Seat: "auditor" when joining seats them as the plan's auditor (read-only).

step.description:
Step is a one-step invite's task, read live (absent when the invite
names none or the task is gone). Its title is teammate text.

used.description:
Used is true when the caller already used this link, or an admin
shared, moved or unshared them while it was live. Accept then answers
shared false if they hold its role now, else 410 graph_invite_used:
ask for a new link rather than asking to join.

status.description:
Status is active until expires_at passes (expired) or an editor
revokes it (revoked, which wins).

totals.description:
Totals is the work routed to any listed group, over every page (q
applied), so a summary never has to add pages up.

unassigned.description: Unassigned is the graph's work routed to no group at all.

done_7d.description: throughput: finished in the last 7 days

needs_review.description: of waiting: a person must act

waiting.description: ready + blocked + needs_review: could move, has not

kind.description:
Kind: guest (an editor made it) or email (a one-tap button in a GVNR
email to a plan member, made by the notifier for that one task).

answered.description: Answered with Answer, LinkURL or FileName when the guest already replied.

note.example: The SDLT figure is from the old offer.

held_by.description: HeldBy is the first name of someone else holding it.

mine.description: Mine: the guest holds it (RunID is their run, to finish it).

sent_back.description:
SentBack: the task was sent back to the link's person to fix (a check
that found something off on their finished work, migration 157), with
what the sender wrote. Shown while it is open and still theirs.

state.description:
State: free (anyone can take it), doing, waiting (finished, waiting
for a yes), done, or later (a step before it is not done yet).

vote_run_id.description:
VoteRunID: the task is waiting for a yes or no on this run, and the
link's person did not do it, so the page offers "Looks good" and "Send
it back" (the vote route still checks they are a judge).

question.description:
Question: send the text as it is (a reply to a GVNR email with no
keyword), not as "I'm stuck: ...".

text.description: Text is what is in the way, 1..300 characters.
text.example: I can't find the March bank statement

can_stuck.description:
CanStuck: "I'm stuck" has someone to go to (the plan's owner, else the
link's maker, never the person themselves).

code.description:
Code: the plan asks for a 6-digit email code before this link acts
(needed), and whether one is out and unused (sent).

email.description:
Email: the link came from a button in a GVNR email (a plan member, by
email). The page names them ("You're Olivia") and their acts read
"Olivia (by email)".

kind.description: Kind is how the plan is drawn (graphs.data.gvnr_kind), when set.

words.description:
Words is the plan's word pack (general, trades, law, events, clinic,
recruiting, sales), absent for general.

note.example: The totals don't match the bank

reason.example: it came from an address we did not send to

status.description:
Status: queued (GVNR sends it within seconds; an address already on
the plan is skipped) or already_sent (sent to this address for this
plan in the last day, so not again).

gates.description: Gates is gate nodes waiting for a decision (looking_for_work).

needs_me.description: NeedsMe is everything waiting on the caller on this plan.

ready.description: Ready is non-gate nodes looking_for_work: claimable now.

running.description: Running is nodes claimed under a live lease.

created_by.description:
CreatedBy and CreatedAt are the acting admin and the time of THIS
request on a write; on the listing they are set only for a legacy row
(v3 exposes no membership timestamp).

group_id.description: GroupID is that group's v3 id — the id gate 3 matches.

group_slug.description:
GroupSlug is the per-DAG v3 group the share is membership of. Absent
for a legacy (not yet folded) per-account row.

username.description:
Display fields exactly as enforcer-v3 returned them to the CALLER on
the listing (after v3's redaction); never stored here.

status.description:
Status is the /access vocabulary for the v3-resolved part of the
listing: ok | unavailable (timeout or 5xx; Retry-After is set) |
forbidden (v3 refused the caller's credential) | unknown_group |
unconfigured (GRAPH_V3_BASE_URL empty). Anything but ok means data
carries only the legacy per-account rows. A graph never shared is ok
with no items and makes no v3 call.

max_turns.description: MaxTurns is the most model turns a run may report (usage.turns).

max_usd.description: MaxUSD is the most a run may report spending (usage.cost_usd).

people.description:
People are first names only, sorted, at most 50. An account with no
first name is "Teammate " and the first 4 characters of its id.

tasks.description:
Tasks are held, waiting, assigned, free, blocked, done, then oldest
first; at most 200.

assigned_to.description: AssignedTo is on assigned only: a first name, or "a group".

blocked_on.description:
BlockedOn is on blocked only: the titles of up to 3 prerequisites not
done yet.

held_by.description: HeldBy is on held only, when the holder is known.

waiting_for.description:
WaitingFor is on waiting only, when an approval seat is open: first
names, and "a group" once for any group seat.

may.description: May is one to three of take, note, finish.

needs_signoff.description: NeedsSignoff: a finish waits for a person's yes. Absent means true.

off.description:
Off is the whole set of kinds to turn off; it replaces the caller's
set. [] turns every kind back on.

every.description: Every is daily, weekly or off. off stops the summary.

tz.description:
Tz is the caller's zone, an IANA name such as Europe/London (the web
app sends Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone). It is the
caller's for every plan: setting it here moves all their summaries.
Omitted keeps the zone they have (UTC if none).

approval.description:
Approval replaces the graph's approval-policy override; its keys win
over the tenant's key by key. An explicit JSON null clears it (inherit
the tenant's); omitted leaves it. An unknown key or a value out of range
is 400 invalid_body naming the key.

client_policy.description: ClientPolicy: off | warn | require (migration 089); omitted leaves it.

confidential.description:
Confidential true makes the plan confidential (migration 115): people
are added by name only. In the same transaction every active invite
link and plan link of the plan is revoked (graph.invite_revoked,
graph.plan_link_revoked), and a validation config with jev true gets
jev false (a config whose only judge was Jev, judges.scope none, is
moved to scope private: the plan's own people judge). false lifts it;
nothing revoked comes back. Omitted leaves it.

context.description:
Context MERGES into the graph's context per key AND per nested key:
{"recall": {"limit": 20}} changes the limit and keeps recall.enabled
(recall and pack are merged separately, not replaced whole). {"recall":
{"enabled": true, "limit": 8}} switches include=recall on a claim on
(limit 1..50, default 8); an unknown key or a bad value is 400
invalid_body naming it. An explicit null resets the whole context to
`{}` and drops the stored context pack bytes; omitted leaves it.

judgment_budget.description:
JudgmentBudget sets the graph's judgment budget (migration 072):
monthly_tokens (required, 1..1e12) bounds the input + output tokens of
judgment attributed to this graph per UTC month, and per_epoch_tokens
(optional, 1..1e12) also bounds them per epoch. A call either would
exceed is skipped with reason graph_budget, as the tenant cap's
token_cap is. An explicit JSON null clears it; omitted leaves it; an
unknown key or a value out of range is 400 invalid_body naming the field.

lifecycle.description:
Lifecycle changes whether the graph ever completes: "terminal" or
"open"; anything else is 400 invalid_lifecycle. open -> terminal on a
graph whose live nodes are all done or cancelled emits graph.completed
(via lifecycle) in the same transaction; terminal -> open while the
graph has an on=completion loop is 400 loop_requires_terminal. Every
change emits graph.lifecycle_changed. Omitted leaves it.

mandates.description:
Mandates replaces the graph's mandates: at most 10, each 1..1000
characters after trimming, blank entries dropped. An explicit JSON null
(or a list with nothing left) clears them; omitted leaves them.

min_client_version.description:
MinClientVersion: X.Y.Z sets it; an explicit JSON null clears it;
omitted leaves it.

node_caps.description:
NodeCaps sets {max_turns, max_usd} (migration 156): a run whose reported
usage (turns, cost_usd) passes one is marked over_cap and opens a
node_over_cap review item. An unknown key or a value out of range is 400
invalid_body naming it; an explicit JSON null clears the caps. Omitted
leaves them.

node_defaults.description:
NodeDefaults REPLACES the graph's per-type node defaults (see
Graph.NodeDefaults); `{}` or an explicit null clears them; omitted
leaves them. Existing nodes are not rewritten: the claim card merges
the defaults at read time.

notify_holds.description:
NotifyHolds true emails every judge hold on the plan (review.opened:
verdict_pending, low_confidence_rejection, verdict_rejected,
verdict_unverified, output_uncertain) to the owner, the task's
assignee and the validation config's arbitrator accounts (migration
150); false stops it. Omitted leaves it.

verification_policy.description:
VerificationPolicy: "advisory" or "gate" sets the override; an explicit
JSON null clears it (inherit the tenant setting); omitted leaves it.

data.description:
Data is merged onto the graph's own metadata — the environment, the
service being built, whatever the caller wants to carry.

lifecycle.description:
Lifecycle overrides the template's: "terminal" (the default) or "open".
Anything else is 400 invalid_lifecycle; "open" on a template that
declares an on=completion loop is 400 loop_requires_terminal.

visibility.description: Visibility defaults to private, matching POST /graphs.

lifecycle.description:
Lifecycle and Loop are what the template or document declared
(docs/REPLAY_AND_QUERY_CONTRACT.md §1, §4); Loop is null when none.

file.description: File is optional: a file the person uploaded to the plan for it.

link.description: Link is optional: an https link that goes with the answer.

text.description: Text is the answer, 1..2000 characters after trimming.

amount_minor.description: AmountMinor overrides the asked amount (the chips: +5, +10).

mode.description: Mode: once (default for a paused task) or ongoing.

share.description: Share: lend (default) or give, for an ask to lend.

you.description: You is the app this request came from, when it named one.

apps.description:
Apps are the approved AI app names, 0..20 of 1..40 characters; an empty
list removes the list (every app is welcome again).

due.description:
Due is optional: when it is needed, YYYY-MM-DD. A question with a due
date put to a guest is a request their AI chases politely.

text.description: Text is the question, 1..1000 characters after trimming.
text.example: Which client file is this for?

to.description: To is the account asked: someone who can see the plan, not the caller.

graph_id.description:
GraphID: more for this plan. AgentID: more pocket money for this bot
(a bot asks for itself with neither).

to.description:
To: owner (the plan's or bot's owner) or team (every other plan with
that much spare, to lend).

period.description: Period: month (plans, the pot) or day (bots).

confirm.description: Confirm a raise that more than doubles the budget.

currency.description: Currency is the caller's locale's, used once to set the workspace's.

mode.description:
Mode: once (this period only) or ongoing (from now on). Default:
ongoing for to_minor, once for add_minor.

no_limit.description: NoLimit ticks or unticks No limit.

to_minor.description:
To sets the budget (minor units); Add raises it (negative lowers).
Give one, or neither with no_limit.

waiting_owner.description:
WaitingOwner: a big raise asked for from an AI app changed nothing; it
is an ask the owner approves on the Money page.

drawn_at.description: DrawnAt is null when no card was drawn for the caller on this plan yet.

daily_line_on.description: DailyLineOn is the date (YYYY-MM-DD, the person's own day) the daily line was last shown, or null.

last_plan.description: LastPlan is null before the first, or when that plan is archived or no longer visible.

undo_until.description: UndoUntil is when the Undo button goes, for the caller's own change.

action.description: Action is the step it became: checked or flagged.

of.description: Of is the account whose work was checked (the task's finisher, else the author of its newest finding).

question_id.description: QuestionID is the question the note became (off on a finding only).

sent_back.description:
SentBack: off on a finished task reopened it and gave it back to Of
with the note (data.gvnr_sent_back); no question was made.

note.description: Note says what is off, 1..1000 characters; required for off, ignored for right.
note.example: The price is per kilo, not per tonne.

verdict.description: Verdict is right ("Looks right") or off ("Something's off").

label.description:
Label is what the firm is to this guest, 1..40 characters ("accountant",
"solicitor"); empty means their AI names the person who asked.

tasks.description: Tasks are 1..40 task titles, each 1..200 characters after trimming.

kind.description:
Kind: choice (recorded as a decision), signoff (a yes on finished
work) or sent_back (a no, with what needs fixing).

seq.description: Seq is a sign-off's place in the plan's chained record.

task.description: Task is the task's title, when there is one the caller can see.

why.example: The auditor confirmed they are out of scope this year.

node_id.description: NodeID is optional: the task it is about.

title.description: Title is the choice, 1..200 characters ("Drop the Q3 accruals review").

why.example: The auditor confirmed they are out of scope this year.

kind.description:
Kind is how the plan is drawn: event (a running order), build (a
blueprint), route (a route map), ledger (a checklist ledger) or board.

files.description: Files are at most 3 photos, scans or PDFs to draft from.

notes.description:
Notes is pasted text to draft from (an email, meeting notes, a list,
or a Word or text file read by the page), at most 20000 characters.
notes.example: Hi all, for Friday we need the venue booked...

sentence.description:
Sentence is what the person wants to get done, 1..500 characters.
It may be empty when notes or files are given.
sentence.example: A garden party for 30 people in June

parallel.description:
Parallel marks a step that can run alongside the step before it; every
other step waits for the one before when the plan starts (link-steps).
The page asks "Does this wait for the step before?" and flips it.

promise.description:
Promise is the deal's own words this step delivers, when the notes
were a deal, proposal or sales email (batch C, sales to delivery).
Teammate text: show it quoted.
promise.example: Two rounds of revisions on the homepage

why.example: Rain plans are the step most garden parties skip

body.description: Body is the new text, 1..4000 characters after trimming.
body.example: Sent the draft to Ada and Bob.

more.description: More: the plan has more steps than the pack holds (5000).

text.example: The bank feed drops transactions after 6pm on Fridays.

you.description: You: the caller is finance (an admin always is).

text.example: Draft by the GVNR helper: Hi all, ...

amber.description: Amber only when the forecast crosses the budget.

line.example: At this pace: £40 of £100 by 30 Nov

next.description: Next is the first task in the handover still open: the next step.

note.example: The bank feed is the slow one.

text.example: The bank feed drops transactions after 6pm on Fridays.

skipped.description:
Skipped says why nothing moved on this plan: not_on_plan (Sara cannot
see it, or either of them is a client seat there), not_admin (someone
else's work, and the caller is no admin), cannot_edit (the caller only
views the plan).

from.description:
From is whose work moves; empty is the caller. Someone else's work
moves only on plans the caller is an admin of.

graph_id.description: GraphID narrows the handover to one plan.

note.description: Note is optional, for Sara: anything she should know.
note.example: The bank feed is the slow one.

to.description: To is who takes the work over: someone on the plans.

until.description:
Until is when they are back, in their words ("Monday"); empty when
they are not coming back to it.

note.description: Note is the last progress note on it, quoted teammate text.

state.description: State is where it stands now: doing, waiting, done or free.

was_held.description: WasHeld: they were doing it when it moved (not only given it).

note.description: Note says why the older version was right (1..500), kept in the decision register.
note.example: The client agreed the February prices for this order.

client.description: Client: the caller sees this plan through the client lens.

label.description: Label is the caller's own seat label when Client.

waits.description:
Waits says whether this step waits for the step before it. Default
true; false for a step that runs alongside the one before (a recipe or
draft step marked parallel, or the owner's "No"). Ignored on the first.

k.description:
K is led_to / new_plans: new plans each plan started this week has led
to so far (the viral coefficient of this week's cohort; recent weeks
keep growing).

led_to.description: LedTo: loop plans so far whose source plan was started this week.

loop_plans.description:
LoopPlans: first plans started this week by people who first met GVNR
through someone else's plan (invite, teammate seat, guest or
email-only link).

loop_share.description: LoopShare is loop_plans / new_plans (0 when no new plans).

new_plans.description: NewPlans: plans started this week, by anyone.

message_ids.description:
MessageIDs marks only these; empty marks every mention of the caller on
the plan.

author_account_id.description: AuthorAccountID is who wrote it: a person, or an agent's service account.

body.description: Body is the message, "" once deleted.
body.example: Sent the draft to Ada for a look.

mentions.description: Mentions are the accounts the message names.

parent_id.description: ParentID is the top-level message this one replies to.

reply_count.description: ReplyCount is the live replies to a top-level message.

unread.description:
Unread is true when the message names the caller and they have not
marked it read.

via.description: Via is the AI app a person wrote through, or the agent's client, when known.

post.description:
Post is true when the caller may write here (an editor or above,
not a client seat).

read.description:
Read is false for a client seat: the discussion is the team's, and
a client's channel is requests (the data is empty, never an error).

next_before.description: NextBefore is the `before` for the next (older) page; null at the start.

unread_mentions.description:
UnreadMentions is how many live messages on this plan name the caller
unread (all of the plan, whatever the filters).

period.description: Period: month (plans, the pot) or day (bots).

share.description: Share: lend (default; the unspent part comes back) or give (for good).

change.description:
Moved: the change, when the caller could give from from_jar. Asked:
the ask its owner got, when they could not (nobody takes silently).

line.example: Office move lent £10 to Month-end close.

sha256.description: SHA256 is the file's (or the link's or figure's exact text's) SHA-256, lower-case hex, computed in the browser.

use.description: Use makes it the current version (default true).

finished.description: Finished counts the tasks the caller finished in this workspace.

guest.description: Guest: joined a plan here from an invite and started none here.

welcome.description:
Welcome lists the plans the caller is new to (shared with them, not
theirs, nothing done on them yet, an open task, not welcomed yet),
newest first, at most 3: their AI's first brief there is "here's
what's yours today, why it matters, and who to ask". POST
/gvnr/nudges/welcome/{graphId}/seen once it was shown.

set.description: Set: this workspace is a partner (it named itself).

joined_at.description: JoinedAt is the first time someone used one of the client's invites.

contact_name.description: ContactName is who the invite is for (1..60), when known.

name.description: Name is the client team (1..80 characters).

pack.description:
Pack is the recipes the team is set up from: starter:<slug> or a team
recipe id, at most 12.

due_soon.description: DueSoon counts tasks due within 3 days that nobody has taken.

state.description:
State: on_track, needs_a_look (something due soon with nobody on it)
or behind (something overdue).

invite_id.description: InviteID is a plan invite made for the client (POST /graphs/{id}/invites).

name.description: Name is the firm's name as clients see it on its recipes (1..60).

note.description: Note is the calm one-liner under the meter, when there is one.
note.example: No limit set. You'll still see what it uses.

pot_left_minor.description:
PotLeft: what is left in the team pot this month (owners and finance;
absent with no pot).

receipt.description:
Receipt: the bots' spend lines on this plan this month, newest first
(at most 100), for the till receipt. Bots are open; people's lines
never appear here.

body.description: Body is the message, 1..4000 characters after trimming.
body.example: Sent the draft to Ada for a look.

mentions.description: Mentions are up to 20 account ids of people on the plan.

node_id.description:
NodeID puts it on one task of the plan (graph-level route only; the
task route takes it from the path).

parent_id.description: ParentID makes it a reply to a top-level message of this plan.

daily_line_on.description: DailyLineOn is the day (YYYY-MM-DD) the daily line was shown.

last_graph_id.description: LastGraphID is the plan the caller is on now. They must be able to see it.

day.description: Day is 1..28 for monthly, 1..7 for weekly (1 = Monday). Ignored for off.

every.description: Every is monthly, weekly or off (off stops it).

tasks.description:
Tasks are 1..40 titles of 1..200 characters. Omitted: the plan's
current task titles (at most 40, in the plan's order).

url.description:
URL is a Slack incoming webhook (https://hooks.slack.com/services/...),
a Teams connector (https://<name>.webhook.office.com/...) or a Teams
workflow (https://<region>.logic.azure.com/workflows/...). It is never
shown again.

answer_file.description: AnswerFile is a file uploaded to the plan with the answer.

answer_link.description: AnswerLink is an https link given with the answer (a document, a folder).

due.description: Due is when the asker needs it (YYYY-MM-DD), for a request to a guest.

text.example: Which client file is this for?

blurb.example: Invites, food, chairs and a plan for rain.

shift_handover.description:
Starters only, what their plans use (batch C): ShiftHandover asks the
three end-of-shift questions, Scorecard has interviewers file a
scorecard, FromDeal turns a pasted deal or proposal into delivery
steps with owners.

slug.description:
Starters only: Slug names its public page (/gvnr/recipes/<slug>),
Industry and Blurb describe it, and PlanKind is how its plan is drawn
(event, build, route, ledger or board).

version.description:
Team recipes (batch C): Version counts approved changes (1 as saved),
UpdatedBy and UpdatedAt say whose suggestion changed it last ("recipe
updated by Sam"), and Brand is the workspace's partner name, so a
partner's recipes carry it ("by Hughes & Co").

words.description:
Words is the word pack a plan from this starter uses (graphs.data.gvnr_words):
general, trades, law, events, clinic, recruiting or sales. Display only.

gotcha.description: Gotcha marks a step most people forget (starters only); Why says what it saves.

parallel.description:
Parallel marks a step that runs alongside the step before it rather
than waiting for it: a plan started from the recipe links every other
step to the one before (POST /graphs/{graphId}/link-steps).

phase.description: Phase groups steps (starters): a stage, a room or a part of the day.

signoff.description: Signoff names who says yes to this step before it counts (starters).

usual_role.description:
UsualRole is who did the task: plan owner, teammate, guest, bot, or
anyone when nobody is recorded.

why.example: Rain is what most garden parties forget

work_steps.description:
WorkSteps is how many recorded steps (took, noted, finished...) the
task took in the plan the recipe came from, or a typical number for a
starter. Absent for a template typed by hand.

data.description: Data is teams per recipe slug, only for slugs used by at least 3.

day.description:
Day is 1..28 of the month (monthly) or 1..7 of the week, 1 = Monday
(weekly).

next_at.description:
NextAt is when the tasks are next added: 07:00 on the next scheduled
day in the plan owner's summary zone (UTC if they set none).

tasks.description:
Tasks are the titles added each time; each gets " (Nov 2026)" (monthly)
or " (w/c 2 Nov)" (weekly) after it.

done.description: Done counts the tasks that reached done in the replay.

first_look.description:
FirstLook: the caller had not looked at this plan before (since is a
week back).

more.description: More: there were more steps than the replay holds; it shows the newest.

by_email.description:
ByEmail: the person acted from a one-tap button in a GVNR email (an
email link, no AI): every surface shows "Sam (by email)". Absent otherwise.

by_reply.description:
ByReply: the person acted by replying to a GVNR email ("DONE, see
attached"): every surface shows "Stacey (by email reply)".

doc.description:
Doc is the document a used_document or kept_version step names
(migration 129): its fingerprint is in the step's hash.

guest.description:
Guest is the name on the guest link the step was taken through (no
sign-in): every surface shows "Olivia (guest link)". Absent otherwise.

client.description:
Client: the caller sees this plan through the client lens; Label is
what the firm is to them.

task.description:
Task is the task's title when the caller can see the task (a client
sees only shared tasks), else null.

text.example: Please upload the March bank statement.

instruction.description: Instruction is the change in the person's words, 1..300 characters.

include_findings.description: IncludeFindings is the plan owner's yes to keep what the team found.

name.description: Name is 1..80 characters after trimming; absent means the plan's name.

candidate.description: Candidate is who was interviewed (1..80 characters).

concerns.example: Wants to work from home four days

node_id.description: NodeID is the interview task, when there is one.

skills.description: Skills: "How did they do on the skills you checked?"
skills.example: Strong on Excel and month-end; rusty on VAT returns

strengths.description: Strengths: "What would make them great here?"

for_client.description:
ForClient true shares it with the plan's client seats; false makes it
internal again.

kind.description: Kind is what item_id names: a task, a note (observation) or a decision.

for_client.description: ForClient is the item's state after the call.

rebalance.description: Rebalance: finance can move between any jars directly.

period.description: Period: month (plans, the pot) or day (bots).

yours.description: Yours: the caller can give from it (owner or finance).

done.description:
Done, Open and Watch are the three answers (each up to 1000
characters); at least one is needed.
done.example: Room 3 cleaned, two deliveries signed for

open.example: Mrs Taylor's prescription is with the pharmacy

watch.example: The back fridge runs warm after 9pm

ask.description: Ask: ask the owner for more (anyone else on the plan).

change.description: Change: raise, lower, top up and tick No limit (owner or finance).

amount.description:
Amount in major units of currency (a vendor's bill: dollars). 0 with
stopped records a run GVNR stopped.

label.description: Label is the receipt line ("Drafted 3 replies"), up to 80 characters.

source.description:
Source for a person: session (a coding session) or api_key. A bot is
always bot.

line.description:
Line: "Paused at £20. Keep going?" while paused; "Owner added £10.
Carrying on." once an ask was said yes to (the newest in the last
hour); empty otherwise.

waste.example: Less waste, not less AI: GVNR stops runaway runs, and your statement shows what it stopped.

by_email.description:
ByEmail: the person acted from a one-tap button in a GVNR email (an
email link, no AI): every surface shows "Sam (by email)". Absent otherwise.

by_reply.description:
ByReply: the person acted by replying to a GVNR email ("DONE, see
attached"): every surface shows "Stacey (by email reply)".

doc.description:
Doc is the document a used_document or kept_version step names
(migration 129): its fingerprint is in the step's hash.

guest.description:
Guest is the name on the guest link the step was taken through (no
sign-in): every surface shows "Olivia (guest link)". Absent otherwise.

line.example: Runs stopped this month: 3 loops, 11 duplicate jobs

can_decide.description: CanDecide: the caller owns the recipe or is a workspace admin.

kind.description:
Kind: add a step (title) after step_index (-1 puts it first), rename
step step_index to title, or remove step step_index. Steps count from 0.

title.example: Check the client's ID before the engagement letter

why.example: We were caught out on the Henderson file

version.description: Version is the version number ("v3" and "3" both work).

host.description: Host is the receiving service's host name, never the url.

approval.description:
Approval is the tenant's approval policy (docs/OUTPUTS_AND_LINKS_CONTRACT.md
§10): how many judgment samples, how they aggregate, what is uncertain
and who is asked then. Keys absent take the defaults; a graph's own
approval overrides it key by key. Always present; `{}` is every default.

has_tenant_key.description:
HasTenantKey says whether the tenant brought its own Jev key. The key is
write-only and is never returned.

mandates.description:
Mandates are criteria appended to EVERY run's frozen acceptance list in
this tenant, after the node's own and the graph's (migration 040), and
judged like any criterion. A node author cannot remove them. Always
present; `[]` when none. Each one is a judged question on every
verification call, so ten mandates are ten more on the token meter.

monthly_token_cap.description:
MonthlyTokenCap is total (input + output) tokens per calendar month (UTC);
0 is unlimited. A call is refused when it would take usage past it.

tokens_used_this_month.description:
TokensUsedThisMonth is the sum of judgment_usage input + output tokens for the
current calendar month (UTC), the figure MonthlyTokenCap is compared to.

verification_policy.description:
VerificationPolicy is the tenant's policy as it applies to a graph with
no override of its own: the tenant's choice, or the platform default
(gate, migration 090) when the tenant never made one.

verification_policy_source.description:
VerificationPolicySource says which: `tenant` (this tenant chose it) or
`default` (no choice stored; the platform default applies, and follows
it if it ever changes).

approval.description:
Approval replaces the tenant's approval policy. Omitted (or null) keeps
it; `{}` resets every key to its default. Unknown keys and out-of-range
values are 400 invalid_body with a detail naming the key.

mandates.description:
Mandates replaces the tenant's mandates: at most 10, each 1..1000
characters after trimming; blank entries are dropped, `[]` clears them.
Omitted (or null) keeps the current list, so a client written before
mandates existed does not wipe them on every save.

model.description:
Model defaults to jev-latest and must match ^jev-. It is resolved to the
versioned id at save time and stored versioned.

tenant_key.description:
TenantKey is WRITE-ONLY. Omitted keeps the current key; the empty string
clears it (the platform key is used instead); any other value replaces
it. Stored as ciphertext; never returned, never logged.

verification_policy.description:
VerificationPolicy is the tenant's choice. Omitted or null stores no
choice: the platform default applies (gate since migration 090), so a
client that enables judgment without naming a policy gets the one
under which a rejection fails the node.

budget.description:
Budget is the graph's own judgment budget (migration 072) and what it
has spent against it: graph route only, absent when the graph has no
budget. Unlike cap it is shown to any viewer: it is the graph's
setting and the graph's spend, which this route already reports.

cap.description:
Cap is always present on the tenant route; on the graph route it is
null unless the caller holds tenant read (the tenant route's gate).

from.description: From and To are the resolved half-open window [from, to), RFC 3339 UTC.

graph_id.description: GraphID is set on the graph route only.

groups.description:
Groups: group_by=day lists every local day in the window, oldest
first, zero-filled; the other keys list keys with usage, most tokens
first, at most 500.

estimated_usd.description:
EstimatedUSD is input_tokens x estimate.price_per_mtok_usd / 1e6,
rounded to 8 decimals. An estimate, never an invoice.

graph_name.description: GraphName is the graph's name, group_by=graph only; absent for null.

key.description:
Key is the group's value: a local date YYYY-MM-DD in tz (group_by=day),
a feature, a model, a graph id or a run id. null is "not attributed":
a usage row with no graph (every row recorded before migration 068, or
a call made for no graph), or with no run (rank, align).

node_id.description: NodeID is the run's node, group_by=run only; absent for null.

resets_at.description: ResetsAt is the next 1st of the month, 00:00 UTC.

tokens_used_this_month.description:
TokensUsedThisMonth is GET /settings/judgment's tokens_used_this_month,
from the same statement: every row of the month, attributed or not.

unattributed_tokens.description:
UnattributedTokens is the part of tokens on rows with no graph (every
row recorded before migration 068 among them). Tenant route only.

external_id.description:
ExternalID is the thing's id in its own service. It may be a URL or a
name, and is never copied into activity metadata.

external_type.description: ExternalType with System names the adapter that types this link.

graph_id.description: GraphID is stamped from the node by the database; a caller never sets it.

role.description:
Role: projection (the thing mirrors this node), gate (it must be
finished before this node passes; a check names the link) or reference
(informational). A node cannot hold a projection and a gate into one
system.

body.example: The prefix hash is the cache key.

evidence.description:
Evidence is what shows this fact is real: the same shape a run's evidence
takes (migration 022/023). Captured by the harness from its own tool
results, not written by hand — an assertion about an assertion is not
support. Optional: a fact with no evidence is stored and labelled
`asserted`, never refused, because a decision has no evidence to give.

kind.description: Kind classifies the fact; default finding.

source.description:
Source is free-text provenance — a document id, URL or run id — so a fact
can be traced back to what produced it.

created.description: Created is every new node, in the order given.

edges_added.description:
EdgesAdded counts every edge written: the subgraph's own, the roots'
inherited prerequisites, and the parent's new dependence on the leaves.

roots.description:
Roots inherited the parent's prerequisites; Leaves are what the parent now
requires. A single-node expansion is both.

severity.description:
Severity is "error" for a line that cannot be right (a placeholder no
runner can satisfy) and "warning" for everything else. A prose line on a
node judged by design has no command or quoted literal: a warning.

assignee.description:
Assignee is whose work the node is (migration 043, contract §10):
present when either half is set. ADVISORY: `for=me|mine` on the
frontier and the claim narrow by it; nothing refuses a claim over it.

attention.description:
Attention rides only with include=attention on listNodes: why this
node waits on the caller (NodeAttention). Absent when nothing does.

claimed_by.description: ClaimedBy is the running run's created_by: the account that claimed it.

claimed_by_name.description:
ClaimedByName is claimed_by's display name ("First Last", else the
username) from enforcer-v3's directory. Absent when the caller is not
shown names (a fine scope or a portal link), the account is in another
tenant, or the directory could not be read. Never scanned: NameClaims
sets it after the read.

lease_expires_at.description:
LeaseExpiresAt is set only while the node is running, and is the deadline
its harness must heartbeat past. Read-only: it is written by claim and
heartbeat, never set directly.

lease_seconds.description:
LeaseSeconds overrides how long a claim holds this node before another
harness may take it. NULL means the graph's default_lease_seconds.

Per node, not one constant, because the right number is not uniform: a
lease short enough to free a flaky test quickly is one that steals a
deploy out from under a live harness (migration 010).

not_before.description:
NotBefore is the time gate (migration 040): the node is neither on the
frontier nor claimable before this instant, whatever its prerequisites.
Absent when unset. A value in the past gates nothing.

opens_at.description:
OpensAt is when a time-gated node whose prerequisites are met becomes
claimable (its not_before). Set only beside not_yet_available.

rank.description:
Rank is the judged risk/effort the ranked frontier stored
(docs/JUDGMENT_CONTRACT.md §9), exactly as the judge answered. It is raw
here because nodes does not compute priority — traverse does, per read —
and because migration 017's trigger clears it whenever title,
description or data change, so a value present is always about THIS
version of the node.

ready_at.description:
ReadyAt, StartedAt, EndedAt and Usage are the node's own timing and
spend (migration 088): derived facts kept by triggers, never written
by a client. See NodeUsage for why Usage is null, not zero.

reclaimable.description:
Reclaimable: the node is `running` but its lease lapsed — its harness is
presumed dead and the next claim takes it (status stays "running"; the
claim's reclaim path keys on it). Absent when false.

run_id.description: RunID is the running run, for heartbeat and completion.

runner.description:
Runner is the running run's data.runner, as the claim named it
(provenance only; absent when the claim named none).

unblocked_by.description:
UnblockedBy is the prerequisite finished last on a ready node, and who
finished it ("You're up"). Set by listNodes only.

work_state.description:
WorkState: looking_for_work (a seat is open: on the frontier, a lapsed
lease included), claimed (running under a live lease — or no lease at
all, which the nodes_running_no_lease gauge counts), looking_for_validation
(verifying: a verdict or votes pending), looking_for_arbitration
(verifying, and the latest attempt is waiting on a person),
not_yet_available (blocked on a prerequisite, or time-gated: see
opens_at), finished (done or cancelled).

assignee_account_id.description:
AssigneeAccountID assigns the node to an account (a uuid; never looked
up in v3 on write). An explicit null clears it; omitting it leaves it.

assignee_group_slug.description:
AssigneeGroupSlug assigns the node to a group by SLUG, the key group
grants use (1..255 characters, no control characters). An explicit null
clears it; omitting it leaves it. Both halves may be set together.

data.description:
Data is shallow-merged into what an existing key stores; omitting it
keeps the stored payload.

description.description: Description of an existing key is kept when omitted (or empty); a value is written.

lease_seconds.description:
LeaseSeconds overrides the graph default for this node. 30..86400. An
upsert that omits it keeps the stored override.

not_before.description:
